title: Winey Crisp Tunisian Fish Tagine
description: A pescatarian-friendly Tunisian dish that combines the flavors of pickles, wine, and fish in a crispy, wine-infused sauce, perfect for a midnight craving.

ingredients.name: Fish fillets (4-6)
ingredients.notes: White fish such as tilapia or sea bass works well

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.notes: Extra virgin olive oil for cooking

ingredients.name: Pickles
ingredients.notes: Chopped dill pickles for added flavor

ingredients.name: Tomato paste
ingredients.notes: Concentrated tomato paste for added depth

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large clay or ceramic tagine over medium heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add chopped pickles, white wine, chicken broth, tomato paste, cumin, and coriander.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add fish fillets to the tagine and cook for 8-10 minutes, until cooked through.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with lemon wedges on the side.
To make a beurre monte, melt 2 tbsp of butter in a small saucepan over low heat.
Add 1 tbsp of all-purpose flour and cook for 1 minute, until lightly toasted.
Slowly whisk in 1 cup of heavy cream and cook until the sauce thickens, about 2-3 minutes.
Season the beurre monte with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the fish tagine with a dollop of beurre monte on top.
